increments.title: The collector accepts, keeps, persists, serves and announces a run's state
increments.goal: Give the collector an endpoint of its own that accepts a run's backlog state, keep the latest state per run, serve the runs it holds and the full state of one over its JSON API behind the existing authentication, persist it across a restart, and announce every write on the existing SSE stream.
criteria: A POST of a run's state to an endpoint of the collector's own is accepted and identified by the issue the state belongs to; a second POST for the same run replaces what was held for it, so the collector keeps the latest state per run and no history.

The JSON API answers both questions: the runs the collector holds, with what a reader needs to pick one including when each was last written, and the full state of one named run; asking for a run it does not hold answers 404.
The new ingest endpoint and the new read endpoints sit behind the collector's existing authentication and reject an unauthenticated caller exactly as its other endpoints do.
A collector restarted against the same measurement directory still serves the run state it held, persisted the way the sessions it already holds are persisted.
A write to a run's state puts a frame on the existing /api/stream SSE stream that tells an already-connected client which run changed.

tools/argus/README.md documents what the collector now accepts and serves, and tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
npm --prefix tools/argus test exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.

return.summary: The collector gains POST /api/runs, GET /api/runs and GET /api/runs/:id over a latest-state-per-run map in the store, a runs.jsonl stream in the measurement directory, and an `event: run` SSE frame, all behind the existing token gate.
return.plan:
WHAT GETS BUILT

A new concept in the collector: a *run state*. It is one opaque JSON document per run, keyed by an id, replaced on every write, never versioned. Three source modules change (`src/store.mjs`, `src/server.mjs`, `src/persist.mjs`); `bin/argus.mjs` and `src/config.mjs` need no change, because the CLI already attaches persistence on `--persist` and replays it on `--open`.

1. THE WIRE CONTRACT (fix it exactly as written; the recorder increment implements against it)

Ingest:

    POST /api/runs
    content-type: application/json
    { "id": "<run id, optional>", "state": { ...the whole backlog.json... } }

- `id` is the run's identity: any non-empty string, trimmed. When it is absent, not a string, or blank after trimming, the collector falls back to `state.issue` when that is a non-empty string — which is how "identified by the issue the state belongs to" holds without the caller having to invent a second name. When neither yields an id, answer 400 `{"error":"run id required"}`.
- `state` has to be a non-null, non-array object; otherwise 400 `{"error":"run state required"}`.
- A body that is not JSON is 400 with the parse message, and the server keeps serving (the same shape as the existing malformed-OTLP path: catch, log through the injected `log`, `sendJson(res, error.status ?? 400, ...)`).
- Reuse `readBody` (its 32 MB cap applies unchanged) and the existing `decompress` helper for `content-encoding`, so a gzipped push works for free.
- Success is 200 `{"ok":true,"id":"<id>","updatedAtMs":<epoch ms>}`.

Read:

    GET /api/runs        -> { total, items: [ { id, issue, workflow, increments, updatedAtMs } ] }
    GET /api/runs/:id    -> { id, issue, workflow, increments, updatedAtMs, state }  | 404 { "error": "unknown run" }

- The list is ordered latest write first and never carries `state`: it is what a reader picks a run by (which issue, which workflow, how many increments, when it was last written).
- `:id` is percent-encoded by the caller and read with `decodeURIComponent`, exactly like `/api/sessions/:id`. An id containing `/` therefore works (`new URL` leaves `%2F` encoded), but the documented convention is a slash-free id.

2. src/store.mjs

- `DEFAULTS` gains `maxRuns: 100`. It is a store option only — no CLI flag, no env var, no new field on `/api/config`.
- The constructor gains `this.runs = new Map()`, id -> `{ id, issue, workflow, increments, updatedAtMs, state }`.
- `putRunState(id, state, { updatedAtMs = Date.now(), replay = false } = {})`:
  - `this.runs.delete(id)` then `set`, so the Map's insertion order is write order.
  - derives `issue` and `workflow` from `state.issue` / `state.workflow` when those are strings, else `''`; derives `increments` as `state.increments.length` when that is an array, else `0`. Those three shallow reads are the only thing the collector knows about the backlog format — everything else in `state` is held and served exactly as it arrived, unvalidated.
  - evicts from the front (`this.runs.keys().next().value`) while `this.runs.size > this.options.maxRuns`, so the least recently written run goes first.
  - emits `{ kind: 'runState', runId: id, run: entry, replay }` through the existing `#emit`, and returns the entry.
- `listRuns()` returns `{ total, items }`, items built from `[...this.runs.values()].reverse()` and then sorted by `updatedAtMs` descending. The `reverse()` matters: `Array.prototype.sort` is stable, so two runs written in the same millisecond still list the later write first. Each item is the entry without `state`.
- `getRun(id)` returns the entry (with `state`) or `null`.
- `clear()` also clears `this.runs` — `DELETE /api/data` is documented as emptying the store, and leaving run state behind would contradict that.
- The existing telemetry `change` object gains `kind: 'ingest'`, so a subscriber can tell the two kinds of change apart. Nothing else about telemetry ingest changes; in particular `this.seq` is NOT advanced by a run write, so the event tail's `sinceSeq` cursor and the `hello` frame keep meaning what they mean.

3. src/server.mjs

- The existing coalescing subscriber gets an early `if (change.kind !== 'ingest') return;` and destructures inside; a run change must never reach `pending.counts[signal]`.
- A second `store.subscribe` handles run changes: return when `replay` is true or no clients are connected, otherwise write `event: run\ndata: ${JSON.stringify({ id, updatedAtMs })}\n\n` to every client immediately. No coalescing and no timer: a run write happens a handful of times per run, and the frame is the whole point of it.
- `handleRunState(req, res)` is an async function beside `handleIngest`, with the same catch-and-answer wrapper at the call site.
- Routing: inside the existing `if (url.pathname.startsWith('/api/'))` branch, after the `DELETE /api/data` case and BEFORE `if (req.method !== 'GET') 405`, add `if (req.method === 'POST' && url.pathname === '/api/runs')`. That placement leaves the auth gate above untouched (so all three routes are gated for free), and leaves every other method on `/api/runs` answering 405 as today.
- The two read routes go into `handleApi` next to the session routes: the exact-match `'/api/runs'` first, then `pathname.match(/^\/api\/runs\/([^/]+)$/)`.
- Do not touch `/api/config`.

4. src/persist.mjs

- `attach`'s subscriber branches on `change.kind`: `'ingest'` behaves exactly as today; `'runState'` returns on `replay` and otherwise appends `` `${JSON.stringify(change.run)}\n` `` through the existing `#append('runs', [...])`. `#file`, `#stream`, `#rotate` and `#read` are all generic over the name, so `runs.jsonl` / `runs.1.jsonl` rotation and the size cap come free.
- `load(store)` keeps its three-signal loop and then reads the `runs` stream: for each line with a non-empty string `id` and an object `state`, call `store.putRunState(record.id, record.state, { updatedAtMs: record.updatedAtMs, replay: true })`; skip anything else (a torn line is already skipped by `#read`). Every restored run line counts toward the returned total, so the `--open` banner's "replayed N records" stays truthful.
- Latest-wins across a restart falls out of replay order — later lines overwrite earlier ones for the same id. No de-duplication pass, no index.
- `--persist <dir>` only ever writes and `--open <dir>` is what replays, exactly as for sessions: that is what "persisted the way the sessions it already holds are persisted" means here, and the documentation has to say it plainly so nobody expects `--persist` to bring a run back.

5. DOCUMENTATION (same commit)

- `tools/argus/README.md`: add `POST /api/runs`, `GET /api/runs`, `GET /api/runs/:id` to the HTTP API table and note that `/api/stream` now also carries a `run` frame; extend "What comes out of it" with one sentence on run state; add a short subsection giving the accepted payload, the id fallback to `state.issue`, latest-per-run/no-history, the 100-run bound, and that the state is held opaquely; extend "How data is kept" with `runs.jsonl` and the `--persist` writes / `--open` replays split.
  CONSTRAINT: `test-repo.sh` greps every `tools/argus/*.md` for wording that describes a removed argus-ui view. The forbidden patterns are `\btabs?\b`, `\bwaterfall\b`, `overview, *tasks`, `tools table`, `under "Attributes"`, `writes the source under`, case-insensitive, with newlines collapsed to spaces. Do not use the word "tab" anywhere in these pages.
- `tools/argus/CLAUDE.md`: one entry under Conventions saying the collector holds a run's state opaquely — latest per run, no history, and the only fields it reads out of it are `issue`, `workflow` and the increment count.
- `tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md` is the test-author's to update (see the test plan).

REJECTED, AND WHY

- A `/v1/runs` ingest path next to the OTLP ones: `/v1/*` is the OTLP spec's namespace on this port and this is not OTLP. The endpoint belongs under `/api/`.
- Feeding run state through `store.ingest()` as a fourth signal: a backlog has no session id, no timestamp window and no attributes; it would land in the session aggregates, the retention windows, the event tail and the facets, all wrongly.
- A separate `subscribeRuns` channel on the store: the store documents exactly one change stream that persistence subscribes to, and a `kind` discriminator keeps that true while making both subscribers explicit about what they handle.
- Folding the run frame into the coalesced `ingest` frame: it would give one frame two unrelated meanings and delay by up to 250 ms the one thing a page waiting on a run write cares about.
- Evicting run states by `retentionMs`: the run being watched is often the oldest thing in the collector by wall-clock time, so an age bound would delete precisely the wrong thing. A count bound is the right one.
- Computing closed/open increment counts in the collector: the status vocabulary (`todo`/`done`/`blocked`/`dropped`) is the recorder's, and the reader that has the full state can count them itself.
- Requiring an explicit `id` with no fallback: it would force the recorder to invent an identity the state already carries, and the criterion asks for identification by the issue.

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS INCREMENT (do not build): the recorder's push in `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs`, and anything under `tools/argus-ui/`.
return.moduleMap:
tools/argus/src/store.mjs — the in-memory store; gains `this.runs` (id -> latest entry), `putRunState`, `listRuns`, `getRun`, the `maxRuns` default, run-clearing in `clear()`, and `kind` on emitted changes. Entry points: `TelemetryStore` class, `subscribe`, `ingest`, `clear`.
tools/argus/src/server.mjs — the HTTP surface; gains `handleRunState`, the `POST /api/runs` route inside the `/api/` branch, the two read routes in `handleApi`, and a second `store.subscribe` writing the `event: run` SSE frame. Entry point: `createServer({ store, token, endpoint, persist, log })`.
tools/argus/src/persist.mjs — append/replay for a measurement directory; `attach`'s subscriber gains the `runState` branch appending to the `runs` stream, and `load` gains the `runs` replay pass. Entry points: `JsonlPersistence` (`attach`, `load`, `close`), `createRunDir`.
tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs — the store's suite; gains the run-state cases.
tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs — the surface's suite; gains ingest, auth, read and SSE cases. Holds `withServer(options, run)`.
tools/argus/test/persist.test.mjs — the persistence suite; gains the round-trip cases and one bin-level restart case. Holds `tmpdir()`, `startCollector()`, `freePort()`, `projectDir()`.
tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md — the suite doc: per-file coverage lines, the helper list, where a new case goes.
tools/argus/README.md — the user-facing page: HTTP API table, "What comes out of it", "How data is kept".
tools/argus/CLAUDE.md — the collector's conventions page.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CODEMAP, for this increment: it is complete for the files I have to change, and two of its entries need no work. `tools/argus/bin/argus.mjs` is not in it and does not need to be — it already constructs the store, attaches `JsonlPersistence` on `--persist` and calls `load` on `--open`, so run state rides those paths untouched. `tools/argus/src/config.mjs` likewise needs no change: the run bound is a store option with a default, not a flag. Everything the codemap lists under `skills/agent-brief/assets/` and `tools/argus-ui/` belongs to the two later increments, not to mine.

return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. `tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md` exists and is accurate for what it describes — one file per module in `src/`, no shared helper module, no mocking library, file-local helpers, lowercase declarative `test(...)` titles, real HTTP on port 0, real filesystem in `mkdtemp` directories. Load it; nothing I read contradicts it. It IS out of date the moment this increment lands, and updating it is one of the increment's criteria: extend the per-file lines for `store.test.mjs`, `server.test.mjs` and `persist.test.mjs` with run state, and add whatever new file-local payload builder you introduce to the "Helpers a new case reuses" list. Note also that `tools/argus/CLAUDE.md` forbids a hard-coded port, forbids asserting a wall-clock duration on a probe path, and asserts messages as absences — all three bind these cases too.

A shared fixture idea, defined file-locally in each of the three files (copy the pattern, per the suite doc): a `backlogState(overrides)` builder returning a backlog-shaped literal — `{ version: 1, issue: 'docs/issues/2026-08-08-x', workflow: 'agile-loop', codemap: '', increments: [ { id: 'one', title: 'First', status: 'todo', note: '', branch: '', steps: [] } ], run: { steps: [] } }` — with `overrides` spread over it. Nothing is mocked anywhere: real `TelemetryStore`, real `createServer` on port 0, real files, real child processes.

I did not run any command; there is no known-red case, and the first run of the list below belongs downstream.

--- CRITERION 1: a POST is accepted, identified by its issue, and a second POST replaces the first ---

1. `store.test.mjs`, unit — a run's state is held under its id and served whole.
   Input/state: fresh `TelemetryStore`; `putRunState('run-a', backlogState())`.
   Expected: `getRun('run-a')` deep-equals the state under `.state`, carries `issue` and `workflow` copied from it, `increments` equal to the number of increments in the state, and a numeric `updatedAtMs`.

2. `store.test.mjs`, unit — a second write for the same run replaces the first, and no history is kept.
   Input/state: two `putRunState('run-a', ...)` calls with different states.
   Expected: `getRun('run-a').state` is the second one, `listRuns().total` is 1.

3. `server.test.mjs`, integration — POST /api/runs accepts a run's state and answers with the id it filed it under.
   Input/state: `withServer({}, ...)`; POST JSON `{ id: 'run-a', state: backlogState() }`.
   Expected: 200; body `{ ok: true, id: 'run-a', updatedAtMs: <number> }`; `store.getRun('run-a').state` deep-equals what was sent.

4. `server.test.mjs`, integration — a POST that names no id is identified by the issue in the state it carries.
   Input/state: POST `{ state: backlogState({ issue: 'docs/issues/2026-08-08-x' }) }` with no `id` field.
   Expected: 200 with `id === 'docs/issues/2026-08-08-x'`, and `GET /api/runs/${encodeURIComponent('docs/issues/2026-08-08-x')}` answers 200 with that state.

5. `server.test.mjs`, integration — a second POST for the same run replaces what the collector held.
   Input/state: POST the same id twice with different states.
   Expected: `GET /api/runs/run-a` carries the second state; `GET /api/runs` has `total === 1`.

6. `server.test.mjs`, integration (edges) — a POST with neither an id nor an issue, and a POST that is not JSON, are both 400 and the collector keeps serving.
   Input/state: POST `{ state: { increments: [] } }` (no id, no issue); then POST the literal body `'{not json'`.
   Expected: 400 for each; `GET /api/health` is 200 afterwards; `GET /api/runs` has `total === 0`.

--- CRITERION 2: the JSON API answers both questions, and 404s for a run it does not hold ---

7. `store.test.mjs`, unit — listRuns names each run with what a reader picks by, latest write first, and never the state.
   Input/state: `putRunState('run-old', ..., { updatedAtMs: 1_000 })` then `putRunState('run-new', ..., { updatedAtMs: 2_000 })`.
   Expected: `items` are `['run-new', 'run-old']` in that order; each item carries `id`, `issue`, `workflow`, `increments`, `updatedAtMs`; no item has a `state` property.

8. `store.test.mjs`, unit (edge: empty) — getRun for a run nobody wrote is null.
   Expected: `getRun('nope')` is `null` and `listRuns().total` is 0 on a fresh store.

9. `store.test.mjs`, unit (edge: limit) — past maxRuns the least recently written run is dropped.
   Input/state: `new TelemetryStore({ maxRuns: 2 })`; write `a`, write `b`, write `a` again, write `c`.
   Expected: `getRun('a')` and `getRun('c')` are held, `getRun('b')` is null, `listRuns().total` is 2 — the re-written `a` counts as the most recent, not the oldest.

10. `store.test.mjs`, unit — clear() drops the run states along with everything else.
    Input/state: put one run state, then `clear()`.
    Expected: `listRuns().total` is 0 and `getRun(...)` is null; a subscriber attached before `clear()` is still attached (assert it still receives a later run change), matching the existing `clear()` case's guarantee.

11. `server.test.mjs`, integration — GET /api/runs lists the runs held and GET /api/runs/:id serves one whole.
    Input/state: POST two different runs.
    Expected: `GET /api/runs` has `total === 2`, both ids present, each item with a numeric `updatedAtMs` and without `state`; `GET /api/runs/<id>` answers 200 with `state` deep-equal to what was posted for that id.

12. `server.test.mjs`, integration (edge) — GET /api/runs/:id for a run the collector does not hold is a 404.
    Expected: status 404 and a JSON body carrying an `error`.

13. `server.test.mjs`, integration (edge) — a method the run endpoint does not take is still a 405.
    Input/state: `PUT /api/runs` (or `DELETE /api/runs`).
    Expected: 405 — the new POST branch must not have opened the method gate for everything else.

--- CRITERION 3: both the ingest and the read endpoints sit behind the existing authentication ---

14. `server.test.mjs`, integration — the run endpoints are gated exactly like the rest of the API.
    Input/state: `withServer({ token: 'secret' }, ...)`.
    Expected: without a credential, `POST /api/runs` (valid body), `GET /api/runs` and `GET /api/runs/run-a` each answer 401 with a `www-authenticate` header, exactly as `/api/sessions` does; with `authorization: Bearer secret` the POST is 200 and `GET /api/runs` is 200; with `?token=secret` on the query string `GET /api/runs` is 200 — both credentials the collector already accepts.

--- CRITERION 4: a restart against the same measurement directory still serves the run state ---

15. `persist.test.mjs`, unit — a run's state survives a restart.
    Input/state: store A with `JsonlPersistence(dir).attach(...)`; `putRunState('run-a', backlogState())`; settle (the file-local 50 ms `settle()`); close. Store B with a fresh `JsonlPersistence(dir)`; `await load(store B)`.
    Expected: `load` counts the run line in its returned total; `store B.getRun('run-a').state` deep-equals the original and `updatedAtMs` is the one that was written, not a fresh clock reading.

16. `persist.test.mjs`, unit (edge: repeat) — two writes of one run replay as one run holding the latest state.
    Input/state: write `run-a` twice with different states before the restart.
    Expected: after `load`, `listRuns().total` is 1 and the state is the second one.

17. `persist.test.mjs`, unit (edge) — a replayed run state is not written back to disk.
    Input/state: attach to a store, then `putRunState('run-a', ..., { replay: true })`, settle, close.
    Expected: `runs.jsonl` does not exist in the directory — the mirror of the existing 'replayed records are not written back to disk' case.

18. `persist.test.mjs`, end-to-end (bin level, in the process-level section after the `/* --- */` banner) — a run state written into a measurement is served again by a collector opened on it.
    Input/state: `startCollector({ cwd, args: ['--persist', dir] })`; POST a run state to `${base}/api/runs`; stop that collector; `startCollector({ cwd, args: ['--open', dir] })`.
    Expected: the second collector answers `GET /api/runs` with `total === 1` and `GET /api/runs/<id>` with the state that was posted. This is the criterion's literal wording, and it also pins the documented split: `--persist` writes, `--open` replays. Uses `projectDir()` and the existing `startCollector`/`freePort` helpers; no wall-clock assertion, no hard-coded port.

--- CRITERION 5: a write puts a frame on the existing SSE stream naming the run ---

19. `server.test.mjs`, integration — a write to a run's state puts a run frame on the stream, naming the run that changed.
    Input/state: open `${base}/api/stream` with an `AbortController` and read the `event: hello` frame first (the existing SSE case's pattern); then POST `{ id: 'run-sse', state: backlogState() }`.
    Expected: reading on until the accumulated text contains `event: run`, the frame's data carries `"id":"run-sse"` and a numeric `updatedAtMs`; abort at the end.

20. `store.test.mjs`, unit — a run-state change is announced to subscribers, and a replayed one is marked as replayed.
    Input/state: `subscribe` collecting changes; `putRunState('run-a', ...)`; then `putRunState('run-a', ..., { replay: true })`.
    Expected: the first change has `kind === 'runState'`, `runId === 'run-a'`, `run.state` present and `replay === false`; the second has `replay === true`. This is what keeps the SSE frame and the persistence append off the replay path, and it is cheaper to pin here than through either of them.

--- LEFT UNTESTED, DELIBERATELY ---

- Rotation of `runs.jsonl` at the size cap: the rotation code is shared with the signals and is already covered by 'files rotate once past the size cap'; a second case would test the same lines through a different name.
- The 32 MB body cap and gzip on `POST /api/runs`: both come from `readBody` and `decompress` unchanged, and each is already covered on the OTLP path.
- `/api/config`: untouched by this increment, so its existing cases stand as the guard.
- Concurrency of two simultaneous POSTs for one run: the server is single-threaded per event-loop turn and last-write-wins is the whole contract; a case would assert scheduling, not behaviour.

--- HOW TO RUN ---

Per file, from the repository root: `node --test tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus/test/persist.test.mjs`. Framework: `node:test` with `node:assert/strict`, no runner config.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE — the closed list, run from the repository root, both required to exit 0:

    npm --prefix tools/argus test
    ./test.sh

Nothing else is run. `./test.sh` covers `test-repo.sh` (which is what catches forbidden wording in the changed markdown pages) and every other package's suite; the per-file commands above are for iterating, not for judging.

return.summary: Round 0 of increment 1 (collector) is accepted. Both listed commands were run in one call from the increment branch: `npm --prefix tools/argus test` (179 cases, exit 0) and `./test.sh` (6 suites, exit 0), nothing skipped. Every criterion is met and covered by a test that would fail if the behaviour broke: POST /api/runs takes a state and files it under `id` or, when that is missing or blank, under the `issue` the state names (400 with neither, and on non-JSON); a second POST replaces the first and listRuns stays at one, so no history is kept; GET /api/runs lists id, issue, workflow, increment count and updatedAtMs latest-write-first and never the state, GET /api/runs/:id serves the state whole and answers 404 for a run not held; all three routes sit below the same auth gate as the rest of /api and answer 401 with www-authenticate, tested unauthenticated and authenticated, header and query token; run state persists as its own runs.jsonl beside the signal files, rotating and replaying like them, with latest-line-wins and replayed writes not written back, proven at unit level and bin level (--persist then --open serves the same state); a write emits an immediate uncoalesced `event: run` frame carrying the run id and updatedAtMs to an already-connected /api/stream client. README, tools/argus/CLAUDE.md and test/CLAUDE.md are updated in the same commit and their factual claims check out (the `--persist` never replays claim matches bin/argus.mjs, maxRuns 100 matches the store). Blast radius traced: the store's change stream gained a `kind` discriminator and both subscribers (persist.attach and the two in createServer) filter on it, and there are no other subscribers; clear() now also drops runs, matching the documented meaning of DELETE /api/data; skills/argus/SKILL.md's endpoint table is an explicit subset and is not made stale. Two observations that need no correction: server.mjs line 119 lost a space in an otherwise untouched line (`pending ??={ seq: 0, ...`), inconsistent with the file's other `??=` but behaviourally identical and unflagged by any linter (the project has none); and the README line about --open reopening a measurement is now one long unwrapped line, in a file that already carries longer ones.

increments.title: The recorder pushes the state it just wrote, best-effort and invisible
increments.goal: Make the recorder send the run's state to the configured collector after every write it makes, without changing anything an agent or a workflow sees and without ever costing a run a failure, a wait or a line of output.
criteria: init, record, branch and close each send the state they just wrote to the collector, identified by the issue the state belongs to.
The recorder stays the only writer of backlog.json and keeps its zero dependencies; no agent page and no workflow prompt changes, so how an agent calls the recorder is exactly what it is today.
The collector's address and its token are read from the environment variables the rest of uroboros already uses for that collector, and from nowhere else.
With no collector configured in the environment, the recorder does nothing extra.

A collector that is unreachable, slow or refusing costs the recorder neither a non-zero exit nor a wait beyond a short timeout, and produces no output: the exit codes and the one confirmation line of every subcommand stay byte-identical to today's.
skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md is current for the cases and helpers this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.

increments.title: argus-ui shows a run's backlog state, live and switchable
increments.goal: Give the interface a run view that shows a run's whole backlog state as the collector serves it, opens on the most recently written run, lets the reader switch runs, and updates itself over the collector's SSE stream.
criteria: The view shows, for the run it is showing: the issue and the workflow it belongs to and when it was last written; the increments in the backlog's order, each with its id, title, status, branch and note; a count of how many increments are closed and how many are open; and the codemap.

Per increment it shows the steps recorded so far, each with its label, its time and its return, collapsed to a summary line and expandable to the full return; the run's own steps — the opening cut, each close, the publish — are shown the same way.
The view opens on the run written to most recently, and the reader can switch to any other run the collector holds.
A write to the shown run's state reaches an already-open page live over the collector's Server-Sent-Events stream: no polling, no reload, no manual refresh.
A closed increment reads as closed, with its status and its note, and an increment with no steps renders as the normal state it is rather than an empty panel that looks broken.
argus-ui still imports nothing outside itself and reads no uroboros file; test/independence.test.mjs still guards exactly that rule, covers every module the view adds, and passes.

tools/argus-ui/README.md says what the interface now shows, and tools/argus-ui/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.

return.summary:
Opening cut of docs/issues/2026-08-08-run-state-in-argus-ui, three increments along the three halves the issue itself names: the collector that holds and serves the state, the recorder that pushes it, the interface that shows it. I cut here and not finer because each of the three is a whole deliverable a reader can judge on its own and each lands in a different project with its own suite; cutting inside one of them (store before endpoint, markup before data) would leave halves nobody asked for. I rejected merging the collector and the recorder into one 'the state reaches the collector' increment: it would span two projects and two suites in one review, and the recorder's rules — best-effort, silent, byte-identical output, zero dependencies — are delicate enough to deserve their own verdict. The collector goes first because it is the load-bearing one: it fixes the wire contract (the endpoint, the payload, how a run is identified, what the list and the detail carry) that the other two are written against, so getting it wrong is what the run most needs to learn early. The recorder is second because it is the producer, and it can be judged against a real endpoint once the collector has one. The interface is last because it is the largest surface and the only one that can be judged against real served state.

Where each acceptance criterion went. Recorder criterion 1 (sends after init, record, branch and close; stays the only writer; zero dependencies; no agent page or workflow prompt changes) and criterion 2 (best-effort and invisible; nothing without a collector; no failure, no wait, no stdout; byte-identical exit codes and confirmation line) and criterion 3 (address and token from the environment the rest of uroboros already uses, and nowhere else) are all in `recorder`. Criterion 4 (an endpoint of its own, latest state per run, served over the JSON API, behind the existing authentication) and criterion 5 (survives a restart, persisted like the sessions) are in `collector`. Criterion 7 (everything the run view shows), criterion 8 (opens on the most recently written run, switch to any other), criterion 9 (a closed increment reads as closed, an increment with no steps is normal) and criterion 10 (independence still guarded and passing) are in `ui`. Criterion 11 (documentation of each half current in the same commit) splits by half, which is how it is written: the collector's page and suite docs in `collector`, the interface's in `ui`, and the recorder's suite doc in `recorder`.

Two criteria I split deliberately, and why. Criterion 6 (a write reaches an already-open page live over the SSE stream) needs both ends: `collector` owns putting the frame on the existing stream, `ui` owns the page reacting to it, and the criterion as the issue states it is only provable in `ui` — its criterion there is the whole of it, the collector's is the frame alone. Criterion 12 (`./test.sh` is green) is the standing bar every increment has to leave the repository at, so it is a criterion of all three rather than of the last one only; each states it alongside the one project suite that increment adds cases to.

One code fact the cut turns on and does not settle: exactly which environment variables count as 'the same environment the rest of uroboros already uses for it'. `tools/argus/src/claude.mjs` exports `UROBOROS_OBS_URL` for the endpoint and the collector's token is `UROBOROS_OBS_TOKEN` in `tools/argus/src/config.mjs` and `tools/argus-ui/src/config.mjs`, so the answer looks settled by the code — the `recorder` researcher confirms it rather than choosing it, and no human decision is needed.

One live guard the later increments will meet, found while mapping and worth naming so it is not discovered by a red suite: `test-repo.sh` fails any file under `tools/argus/*.md` that describes an argus-ui view in words the interface no longer uses ('tabs', 'waterfall', 'tools table' among them), so the collector's documentation of the new endpoints must stay about what it serves and say nothing about how the page lays it out.

No push failure: `backlog.json` and this return are committed and pushed on branch claude/argus-workflow-backlog-status-nvqmvr.
